solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note, evangelist's brag!

definitions.meaning: an instruction to pay attention to what follows, as in 'heed this'
playfully, St Mark the Gospel writer boasting about his own Gospel text

explanation.surface: A jotting about a preacher boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is one of the four evangelists, so the stock phrase can be read as that saint proudly claiming the words of his Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to tell a listener to take careful notice of a prediction.

clue.text: Partly open a small bottle

parts.note: a jar is a small container for jam or pickles

explanation.surface: Instructions to open a little flask only partway.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be standing that way, a common synonym.

clue.text: Deity has rink altered

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A god has had his skating rink remodelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindu tradition worships this figure as an avatar of Vishnu, so he is a god.

clue.text: Period in which any earnings are declared

indicators.note: the answer sits within the following words
the letters are openly shown, displayed within the phrase any earnings

explanation.surface: A tax period during which all income must be reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which ... are declared' signals the letters lying in 'anY EARnings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months is a period of time, the length used for tax returns.

clue.text: Objection to son's treatment is not easily understood

parts.note: OB is a dictionary abbreviation of objection
S is the standard abbreviation for son
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: A complaint about a boy's therapy is hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: OB for objection is listed in Chambers; the 's of son's and 'to' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky or abstruse is hard to grasp, the usual sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Boy climbed around Island house

indicators.note: the reversed boy goes round the island letter
in a down clue the word goes upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad clambered round an island building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbed' turns LAD to DAL; 'around' puts it round I. The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative chamber is called a house, and this is Ireland's lower one.

clue.text: Proud as one on stilts

definitions.meaning: holding one's head high with self-respect
literally, someone striding along raised high above the ground

explanation.surface: A stilt-walker looks proud.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means carrying oneself with dignity, while a stilt-walker literally moves about at height.

clue.text: HMS Belfast?

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, and the HMS prefix makes it a ship

explanation.surface: Just the name of the cruiser moored on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Belfast is a museum cruiser in London; the joke reads it as a ship named after a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a major warship such as a battleship or cruiser, and this vessel was a cruiser.

clue.text: Catharine's chewed about five hundred Spanish flies

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the numeral
chewed up means mangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the name and its S are used as letters
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A woman named Catharine munched some blister beetles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' jumbles CATHARINES, and 'about' puts it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish fly is a blister beetle, and its plural is this Latin-derived word, also the dried beetles used medicinally.

clue.text: Rush to purchase grass!

parts.note: panic is a kind of grass, so buying it is a pun on a frantic rush on the shops

explanation.surface: A frantic dash to buy some cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Panic grass is a real cereal grass, so the phrase also means acquiring it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurried stockpiling in fear of shortage is the everyday sense of the phrase.

clue.text: The Spanish interpret curious creed as an example

indicators.note: odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards interpreting an odd religious creed as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: Creed, with a lower-case c to mislead, was a British maker of telegraph machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Creed & Company made printing telegraph machines, so a Creed is one example of the device.

clue.text: A service returned from a distance

indicators.note: sent back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis serve hit back from a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads RAF backwards as FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at or from a great distance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Material from Luxembourg's excellent

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: Fabric from the Grand Duchy is top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: This openwork fabric of thread is a textile, so a material.

clue.text: Girl leaves before rain spreads

indicators.note: the leaves come ahead of the rest

parts.note: kat (khat) is a shrub whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant

indicators.note: the letters spread out into a different order

explanation.surface: A girl departs before the rain sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a noun, the khat plant; 'spreads' turns RAIN into RINA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's first name, so one example of a girl.

clue.text: Operation to remove one stuffed jacket

indicators.note: the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: action is operation, as in a machine in action
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Surgery to take out someone's padded coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An acton was a quilted jacket worn under mail armour, so a padded garment.

clue.text: Endlessly embroider strange platitude

indicators.note: odd, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word loses both its ends

explanation.surface: An order to keep stitching an odd cliché.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' leaves MBROIDE, which 'strange' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, soothing remark is called this, after the sedative salt.

clue.text: Gideon's first in defeat, as Enoch did for Methuselah

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to beat is to defeat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: A biblical tale of Gideon routing foes, set beside Genesis genealogy.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 5 says Enoch fathered Methuselah, using the old verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The King James Bible's archaic past tense of beget, meaning fathered, is used in the Genesis line.

clue.text: A cook's beginning to keep almost all fruit

indicators.note: just the starting letter of the word
the word is used except its last letter

explanation.surface: A chef starting to preserve nearly all the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Caribbean tree fruit eaten in Jamaica with saltfish.

clue.text: Arkwright's active in Japanese drama

indicators.note: the letter for active is placed inside the drama

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama
A is the abbreviation for active, as in grammar

explanation.surface: Richard Arkwright, the mill inventor, performing in a Japanese play.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like the industrial pioneer; here it means a builder of an ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark, so he is literally an ark-builder.

clue.text: Robe tailored for bishop

indicators.note: the garment is cut and re-sewn, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Vestments made to measure for a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor (from Latin Eboracum) is the signature of the Archbishop of York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs using the Latin name of his see, so it stands for that prelate.

clue.text: No lad flies like a knot

indicators.note: moves wildly, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: No boy can fly as a knot does.
explanation.walkthrough: The knot here is also a wading bird, which suits 'flies'.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a node, a point where lines meet, and the adjective means relating to nodes.

clue.text: Fresh arrangement that begins when contract's made

definitions.meaning: a new settlement or agreement, such as Roosevelt's programme
a fresh hand of cards, dealt once a bridge contract has been played

explanation.surface: A new agreement takes effect when a contract is signed.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a contract is the bid declarer must make; once played, the cards are dealt anew.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any new bargain and also, literally, a redealing of the cards.

clue.text: The French decline North American dish

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to sag is to droop or decline

explanation.surface: The French refuse an American meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' suggests refusing, but here means drooping.
explanation.definitionFit: The baked pasta layered with sauce is a dish, here in its Italian-American spelling.

clue.text: Kitchen ordered to give more substance to soup

indicators.note: put in order differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The kitchen was told to make the soup heartier.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding flour or cornflour makes a liquid denser, the cookery sense of the verb.

clue.text: No energy to instruct year about theoretical particle

indicators.note: the energy letter is absent from the verb

parts.note: to teach is to instruct
E is the physics symbol for energy
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Lacking energy to teach a year's course on a hypothetical particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No energy' removes E from TEACH, leaving TACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists hypothesise this particle that would always travel faster than light; none has been detected.

clue.text: Sediment from river with a bit of sludge

parts.note: the Lee is a river, in London and in Cork

indicators.note: only a small piece, the opening letter, of the word is used

explanation.surface: Silt from a river mixed with sludge.
explanation.definitionFit: The dregs settling at the bottom of a wine bottle are a sediment.

clue.text: Bush is pronounced to be boring

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: something slow is dull or tedious

explanation.surface: A shrub declared to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn shrub bears this sour fruit, and the plant itself goes by the same name.

clue.text: Opportunity of seeing stake won

parts.note: vie is an old card-game term meaning to wager or stake
W is the abbreviation for won in sports tables

explanation.surface: A chance to watch a winning bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vie' as a verb once meant to stake money on a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance to see something, as at a private viewing, is called this.

clue.text: Keen to roll joint

indicators.note: rolling the word around jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: Eager to roll a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' invites the drug sense, but it means a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg articulation between thigh and shin is a joint of the body.

clue.text: Cabbage broth is starter in Kinross feast

indicators.note: the opening letter of the place name

parts.note: an ale was a rural festival, as in church-ale

explanation.surface: Cabbage soup as the first course of a Scottish banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinross is a Scottish town; in Scotland kale also means a cabbage broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots use the word both for the curly cabbage and for a soup made with it.

clue.text: Camp bed?

parts.note: not a folding bed but the padded sack one sleeps in at a campsite

explanation.walkthrough: A camp bed is a folding cot; the question mark allows a looser bed for camping.
explanation.definitionFit: This insulated sack serves as the bed when camping outdoors.

clue.text: Lurid reading. Hardly!

parts.note: the directory has ..., lurid in colour, but its contents are dull, not sensational

explanation.surface: Sensational literature dismissed with a scoff.
explanation.walkthrough: Lurid can mean glaring yellow; yellow press means sensational journalism, yet the business directory is tame.
explanation.definitionFit: The classified telephone directory, printed on yellow paper, is reading matter of the dullest sort.
